ground_truth_answer: Under this model, 1,000 Government ITIs will be upgraded in clusters, with 200 Hub ITIs and 800 Spoke ITIs. - State Government: 24.5%

question: What is the “Snehasparsham” scheme?
ground_truth_answer: The Government of Kerala has launched the "Snehasparsham" scheme to protect and help unwed mothers. The problems of unwed mothers are linked with various socio-economic and cultural variables. In Kerala, this problem is coupled with the ignorance and exploitation of the backward classes. It has been pointed out that there are many women in Wayanad and other districts of Kerala who are victims of social exploitation and atrocities and are often forced to become unmarried mothers. The percentage of abortion-related hazards and death is high among teenage unwed mothers.

ground_truth_answer: Both EMR and HRHR projects are expected to address important and challenging issues resulting in advancement of scientific knowledge. However, in HRHR projects, the risks associated to address the proposed scientific issues are high, and if it is successfully solved, should result in high reward. This could be in the form of new hypothesis, methodology, process or products, and may have the potential to open up new frontiers in S&T. In other words, proposals resulting in 'incremental knowledge' will not be supported under the HRHR scheme.

ground_truth_answer: Newly selected villages receive ₹20,00,000/- for Gap-filling infrastructure development activities that cannot be covered through convergence with other schemes. scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram

ground_truth_answer: Villages that successfully implement their Village Development Plan and complete the five-year monitoring period can receive an additional round of funding. question: How many socio-economic developmental indicators must be monitored and across how many different domains are these indicators distributed?
ground_truth_answer: Villages must monitor 50 socio-economic developmental monitorable indicators distributed across 10 domains including drinking water and sanitation, education, health and nutrition, social security, rural roads and housing, electricity and clean fuel, agricultural practices, financial inclusion, digitization, and livelihood and skill development.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram

ground_truth_answer: Villages must achieve a score of 70 or above on the monitorable indicators and be declared as Open Defecation Free to qualify for Adarsh Gram declaration. Each indicator can achieve a maximum score of 2, making the total possible score 100.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram

ground_truth_answer: State Governments and Union Territory Administrations are expected to ensure convergence of at least 3 to 4 times of Gap-filling funds from existing Central and State Schemes or matching grants to achieve comprehensive village saturation with basic infrastructure.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram

ground_truth_answer: The Gram Sabha must undertake social audit of the scheme at least once a year to ensure greater transparency and better utilization of resources, following the same methodology required under Section 17 of the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram

ground_truth_answer: The need assessment requires Format I for village level data, Format II for village level infrastructural needs, Format III-A for family and individual needs, and Format III-B for consolidation. The final Village Development Plan consists of Formats I, IV, V and VI.

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram

scheme_name: Pradhan Mantri Anusuchit Jaati Abhyuday Yojana (PM-AJAY) - Adarsh Gram

To develop clusters of traditional industries in the country over a period of five years.
To make traditional industries more competitive, market-driven, productive, and profitable.
To strengthen the cluster governance systems with the active participation of the stakeholders.
To build up innovative and traditional skills, improved technologies, advanced processes, market intelligence, and new models of public-private partnerships, so as to gradually replicate similar models of cluster-based regenerated traditional industries.

scheme_name: Promotion of Exportable surplus of identified spices in NE: Cultivation of NE ginger (Ha)
question: What is the Promotion of Exportable Surplus of Identified Spices in the North East: Cultivation of Ginger scheme?
ground_truth_answer: The scheme is a financial assistance programme implemented by the Spices Board under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry to encourage ginger cultivation in the North Eastern region of India. It supports farmers by providing subsidy assistance for quality planting material so that production, quality, and export potential of ginger can improve across the region.

scheme_name: Promotion of Exportable surplus of identified spices in NE: Cultivation of NE ginger (Ha)
question: What financial assistance is available under the scheme?
ground_truth_answer: Under the scheme, financial assistance is provided at 50 percent of the cost of planting material used for ginger cultivation. However, the maximum assistance allowed is ₹30,000 per hectare. The remaining expenditure must be borne by the farmer.

scheme_name: Promotion of Exportable surplus of identified spices in NE: Cultivation of NE ginger (Ha)
question: What does the term “planting material” mean in this scheme?
ground_truth_answer: Planting material refers to quality ginger seed rhizomes or certified propagating materials used for cultivation. The scheme encourages farmers to use healthy, disease-free, and high-quality planting material to ensure better yield and improved marketability.

scheme_name: Promotion of Exportable surplus of identified spices in NE: Cultivation of NE ginger (Ha)
question: Is there any minimum or maximum land requirement for eligibility?
ground_truth_answer: Yes, farmers must cultivate ginger on at least 0.10 hectare of land to qualify under the scheme. The maximum eligible land holding covered under the programme is 8 hectares.

scheme_name: Promotion of Exportable surplus of identified spices in NE: Cultivation of NE ginger (Ha)
question: Can small and marginal farmers also benefit from this scheme?
ground_truth_answer: Yes, small and marginal farmers are one of the major target groups of this programme. As long as they meet the minimum land requirement and cultivate ginger in eligible regions, they can apply for financial assistance.

scheme_name: Promotion of Exportable surplus of identified spices in NE: Cultivation of NE ginger (Ha)
question: How is the subsidy amount calculated for farmers?
ground_truth_answer: The subsidy is calculated based on the actual cost incurred for purchasing planting material. Since the assistance covers only 50 percent of the cost, the farmer receives reimbursement up to the prescribed ceiling of ₹30,000 per hectare.

scheme_name: Promotion of Exportable surplus of identified spices in NE: Cultivation of NE ginger (Ha)
question: Which authority is responsible for implementing the scheme?
ground_truth_answer: The scheme is implemented and supervised by the Spices Board through its regional and field offices operating in the North Eastern region.

scheme_name: Promotion of Exportable surplus of identified spices in NE: Cultivation of NE ginger (Ha)
question: Are inspections conducted before approving the financial assistance?
ground_truth_answer: Yes, designated officials conduct field inspections before approving assistance. During inspection, officials verify the cultivated area, use of planting material, and compliance with scheme conditions. Only eligible and verified cases are recommended for subsidy release.

scheme_name: Promotion of Exportable surplus of identified spices in NE: Cultivation of NE ginger (Ha)
question: Can tenant farmers or lease cultivators apply for the scheme?
ground_truth_answer: Tenant farmers or lease cultivators may also apply if they can provide valid proof of cultivation or lease agreements. Final approval depends on verification by the concerned Spices Board authorities.

scheme_name: Promotion of Exportable surplus of identified spices in NE: Cultivation of NE ginger (Ha)
question: What are the major objectives of the ginger cultivation scheme?
ground_truth_answer: The scheme aims to increase ginger production in the North Eastern region, improve the quality of exportable ginger, promote scientific cultivation practices, strengthen spice exports, and improve the income and livelihood of farmers engaged in spice cultivation.

question: What is the emolument provided under the programme?

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.1 What Is AICTE Expecting From The Institution?
ground_truth_answer: A. AICTE expects institutions to fund its other clubs in a similar fashion and intensify their activities. Vibrant clubs will attract the attention of other institutions and inspire the latter to emulate. Thus there will be an intensification of club activities across the country.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.2 What Are The Strong Points Which Enhance The Possibility Of Support From AICTE?
ground_truth_answer: A. Past achievements of the club, its interface with industry/professional body, achievements of the Faculty Coordinator, and Credentials of the institute.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.3 Are Student Chapters/Societies Also Eligible To Apply?
ground_truth_answer: A. Yes.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.4 How Many Proposals Can Be Submitted By The Institute?
ground_truth_answer: A. Institute can seek support for one club only, for which it must be willing to support financially also.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.5 Will My Institute Be Eligible To Apply Again If The Project Is Granted Once?
ground_truth_answer: A. No. Institute will be eligible to receive the grant under the SPICES scheme only once. AICTE expects the institute to support other clubs in a similar fashion.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.6 Can Non-Technical/ Non-Engineering Clubs Apply Under This Scheme?
ground_truth_answer: A. Yes, the club from any discipline/ theme/ stream in an AICTE-approved institution can be proposed under this Scheme, provided it fulfills other eligibility conditions.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.7 What Is The Total Duration To Complete The SPICES Project?
ground_truth_answer: A. It's a one-year project which starts from the date of the Offer Letter/Sanction Letter.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.8 When Does The One-Year Project Duration Start?
ground_truth_answer: A. For the 2020-2021 batch, the date of receipt of funds is reckoned as the date of start of the project which must be intimated to AICTE. However, for those sanctioned in 2021- 2022, the date of the Offer Letter is the date of the start of the project.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.9 If Both Coordinator & Co-Coordinator Are Transferred/ Changed, Then How To Update The Details Of Another Coordinator?
ground_truth_answer: A. The institute must appoint another faculty as a coordinator whose qualifications and experience must be matching with the previous one and take approval from AICTE. One needs to go to "Request for Change of Coordinator/Co-coordinator" on the SPICES Review Portal, attach the requisite documents on the SPICES review portal, duly signed by the Head of Institution, and Coordinator, and submit.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.10 Do We Need To Submit Any Report To AICTE After The Completion Of The Project?
ground_truth_answer: A. Yes, at the end of the project duration, the institute must submit a soft copy and hard copy of the project report and original bills for the closure of the project.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.11 Is There Any Requirement On The Minimum Number Of Activities To Be Conducted Under This Scheme? Can We Conduct One Single Event/Activity?
ground_truth_answer: A. Club must conduct as many activities as possible, spread throughout the year. Club members may be encouraged to raise funds from other sponsors.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.12 Can We Conduct The Event/Activities In The Club Online Mode Or Hybrid Mode?
ground_truth_answer: A. AICTE recommends club activities to be held offline to enhance student interaction between peers and experts invited.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.13 Can We Collaborate With Other Councils/Clubs In Our College To Conduct An Activity?
ground_truth_answer: A. We encourage collaborative activities with not just clubs in your institutions but also with those focussed in your area, in nearby institutions (for example if your club is on Robotics, try collaborating with the Robotics club in a nearby institution). We expect these clubs with whom you shake hands also to reciprocate your gesture. This is equally important. By supporting and focussing on one club under the Scheme, our larger intention is to see other clubs also get energized, that's why your club has been selected to be transformed as a model club. Please document and share the success stories emerging out of such collaborations, with all the beneficiaries under SPICES.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.14 Can We Upload The Details Of The Events/Activity Which Were Conducted Before Receiving The Offer Letter From The Institute?
ground_truth_answer: A. Any activity which was conducted before receiving the Offer Letter will not be acceptable.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.15 Can We Consider Taking Our Students For A One-Day Outdoor Experiential Learning Activity
ground_truth_answer: A. Yes, but the expenditures on account of travel cannot exceed 40%. Additional expenditures, (if any) should be borne by the institute.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.16 We Have Been Sanctioned Project In 2021-2022. When Will The Fund Of Rs. 1 Lakh Will Be Released?
ground_truth_answer: A. Your institute will be reimbursed Rs. 1 lakh once the project is completed, but not before one year. Subject to all other conditions being fulfilled.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.17 What Is The Proportion Of Contribution From The Institute And Support From AICTE Over 100% Of Expenses Incurred On The Student's Club Activities?
ground_truth_answer: A. The total project cost is a minimum of Rs. 2 Lakh with Rs. 1 Lakh from AICTE and the rest coming from the institute (minimum Rs. 1 Lakh). If the expenditure within the project duration is less than Rs. 2 Lakh then a grant from AICTE will be reduced to 50% of actual expenses accrued for the club activities.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.18 Can I Get The Payment In Favor Of The Coordinator’s Account Name?
ground_truth_answer: A. No. The grant can only be released in favor of the Director/ Principal/ Registrar of the institution. Applicant must provide duly-filled mandate form having the seal and signature of the bank authority.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.19 Can The Grant Be Utilized By The Institute On The Expenditures Pertaining To The Faculty Coordinator/ Co-Coordinator Or Any Other Faculty Member?

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.21 Can We Allow Registration Fees To Be Collected From Students For The Event(S)/ Activities?
ground_truth_answer: A. It is up to the institute to decide whether to collect the registration fee or not.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.22 Can We Use The Grant For Publishing Books?
ground_truth_answer: A. The grant can be utilized for the publication/printing of promotional material for events/activities organized by the club.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.23 Visiting Industrial/Technical Hubs Can Be Taken As An Event And Submit The Bills For Consideration.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.24 Are We Allowed To Spend Institute-Committed Funds On Hospitality To Experts, And Participants From Outside Apart From Expenses On Remuneration To Experts, And Prizes To Participants?
ground_truth_answer: A. The funds pooled (AICTE and college) can be used for events and activities organized by the student club to which the project is offered but not for any other club. Not more than 40% of the pooled amount can be used on travel. It can be used to meet the expenses related to experts/ resource persons invited to the events organized by the club.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.25 Our Club Is Selected For The Grant Of Rs. 1 Lakh, And In The Letter, It Is Mentioned That We Can Utilize Its 40% For The Event Registration And Organizing Event, How We Can Utilize 60% Part Of The Grant?
ground_truth_answer: A. Club can utilize 60% amount in event organization expenses viz. publicity, prize money, club merchandise (such as T-Shirts, Cups, etc.)

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.26 Can The Institute Use The Fund Amount For Two More Clubs?
ground_truth_answer: A. Funds under the project granted to your institute (contributed by your institute and AICTE) have to be spent on the Club mentioned in the Offer Letter; and NOT on the other clubs. The funded club will serve as a model to other clubs in the institute, the experience gained and good practices of which can be applied to at least two more student clubs that are to be proposed to us.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.27 What Is The Process Of Refunding The Unspent AICTE Grant? (Valid For 2020-2021 Project Batch)

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students

ground_truth_answer: A. Yes, we recommended promoting activities/events being conducted under the funded club on social media using the #aictespices and #aicte.

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students

scheme_name: AICTE - Scheme For Promoting Interests, Creativity And Ethics Among Students
question: Q.34 Do We Need To Click On The Review Submit Button Every Time After Uploading The Single Event Detail On The SPICES Review Portal?

question: What are the different categories of applicants and how do the benefits differ between them for this literature preservation initiative?

question: What happens if my submitted manuscript contains content that criticizes government policies or makes comments about religious communities?
ground_truth_answer: The Academy reserves the right not to print your book and can refrain from making payment or even recall payments already made if your scripts or lyrics contain adverse remarks against any governments, individuals, institutions, or anything against caste, creed, and religion that may hurt sentiments.

scheme_name: Preservation of Tiatr Literature
question: In what specific language and script format must my manuscript be prepared for consideration under this preservation initiative?
ground_truth_answer: Your manuscript must be prepared in Konkani language written in Roman Script format. All scripts, lyrics, and musical compositions must adhere to this language and script requirement as specified by the Academy.

scheme_name: Preservation of Tiatr Literature
question: How many physical copies of my manuscript do I need to submit along with my application for review?
ground_truth_answer: You must submit 3 typed copies of your manuscript along with your application. Additionally, you also need to provide a soft copy on a Compact Disc, Digital Versatile Disc, or Pen Drive.

scheme_name: Preservation of Tiatr Literature
question: What is the minimum number of book copies that will be printed if my manuscript gets approved for publication?

scheme_name: Preservation of Tiatr Literature
question: If I am currently performing and writing for tiatr productions, which category should I apply under and what benefits can I expect?
ground_truth_answer: As an active tiatr artiste, you should apply under Category II. You will receive 200 copies of your published book, a one-time honorarium fixed by the Academy for each script or anthology, and the Academy will fund the entire publication from its allocated scheme funds.

scheme_name: Preservation of Tiatr Literature
question: Are there any financial documents I need to provide as part of my application submission process?

question: What type of dramatic works are eligible for consideration beyond traditional full-length tiatr productions?

question: If I want to publish my work independently but still receive financial support, what obligations do I have toward the Academy?
ground_truth_answer: Under Category III, you must ensure your book conforms to all scheme norms, provide 100 books to the Academy free of cost, and you will receive 100% printing cost reimbursement but no honorarium payment.

a. In case of Widow applicant a copy of the death certificate of her husband issued by the Registrar- Births & Deaths;

g. A marriage invitation card of the marriage for which the financial assistance is sought. 
h. Self-declaration to the effect that no financial assistance has been received by the applicant from any other Govt. organization, Non-Govt. organization, Municipal Corporation of Delhi or New Delhi Municipal Corporation or any other statutory or non-statutory agency for this purpose. 
i. Aadhar Card 
j. Residence proof of last 5 year residence in Delhi. 
k. Bank account details (Single -operated Aadhar linked) in Delhi only. 
l. Bank passbook / statement for last one year. 
m. In case of SC/ST applicant, caste certificate in the name of the applicant issued by competent authority and in case of minority applicants selfdeclaration of the religion of the applicant duly verified from the religious institution has to be submitted.
n. One passport size photo of applicant. 
o. One photograph of Marriage Ceremony.
